markdown_report:
The best first step is a padding-aware temporal diagnostic for the supplied GRU4Rec. Progress is 0%; establish whether recurrent memory supports next-item ranking before changing training.

**Insights from the starting point**

1. Feedback distinguishes broad relatedness from current usefulness. Interaction histories cannot establish compatibility, redundancy, or mood, so those explanations remain hypotheses.
2. Existing probes measure embedding alignment and sampled training margins. Neither directly establishes held-out ranking quality or useful temporal dependence.
3. Left padding makes representation extraction consequential. Padding invariance and final-nonpadding readout checks should precede behavioral interpretation.

**Insights from related work**

1. [Sampling reliability](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748086) depends on the candidate protocol. Keep official 99-negative validation HR@10 for selection and label diagnostic rankings separately.
2. [CETD](https://www.mdpi.com/2076-3417/13/20/11176) motivates temporally structured counterfactuals. Matched history perturbations can investigate order and recency, but deletion sensitivity alone cannot identify stale memory.
3. [Enhanced BPR](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.19276) addresses false-negative risks. Unobserved alternatives should remain comparison candidates, not verified dislikes.

**Directions and framework**

| Direction | Observable evidence | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|
| Interface correctness | Padding invariance, valid-position readout | Correctness does not establish relevance |
| Temporal utility | Paired target-rank changes | Deletions can create unfamiliar histories |
| Candidate difficulty | Frequency-stratified margins | Frequency does not measure exposure |

**Candidate ideas**

Scores use 0–10; higher difficulty means more implementation effort.

| Idea | Originality: positive / negative | Potential: positive / negative | Difficulty: positive / negative |
|---|---|---|---|
| Paired temporal probe | 4: connects state and rank / familiar perturbations | 8: guides memory changes / exploratory attribution | 3: no retraining / careful batching |
| Frequency-stratified margin audit | 3: contextualizes existing margins / established slicing | 6: exposes uneven separation / limited generalization evidence | 2: reuses hooks / sparse slices |
| Jointly trained recency gate inside GRU | 4: adapts memory retention / overlaps GRU gating | 7: potentially useful adaptation / usefulness unverified | 5: compact layer / retraining and predictor updates |

**Selected algorithm: paired temporal utility probe**

Sample one eligible next-item example per user strictly within training histories. Score its target against a fixed diagnostic candidate set under intact history, equal-count recent/older/random deletion, and local shuffling that preserves the final item. Repack survivors chronologically and left-pad. Report target-rank changes, diagnostic HR@10 changes, final-state cosine distance, sample counts, and paired user-bootstrap intervals. State displacement without ranking damage is insufficient evidence of predictive importance.

Preserve `DiagnosisProbe(view, device)`, `run_full_diagnosis(train_loader)`, and `diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis)`. Missing measurements return null with an explicit reason. Keep unavailable metadata breakdowns empty. This probe evaluates each existing category checkpoint without fitting additional predictors; official validation remains unchanged. No improvement is claimed before measurement.

idea.description: Add a paired temporal utility probe to the family-specific GRU4Rec diagnostic adapter, measuring how controlled history changes affect both recurrent states and next-item rankings.
idea.motivation: The qualitative feedback suggests weak alignment with recent intent, but current training-margin probes cannot determine whether useful temporal information reaches the ranking output. At 0% research progress, a controlled diagnostic is a feasible way to choose the next training experiment.
idea.implementation_notes: Use only training-history prefixes and their next interactions; never access test labels. Preserve the corrected GRU4Rec backbone, all four category routes, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, and the supplied training limits. Use the actual view.model in evaluation mode under torch.no_grad(), restoring its prior mode afterward. Retain log2feats(sequence), item_emb, and predict_score(features, items). Extract final features using the maximum index whose item ID is nonzero, never nonpadding_count minus one; exclude empty prefixes. First compare an identical history with different amounts of leading padding where the interface permits. For deletion comparisons, use the same deletion count and retain the original final item; report this conditional design explicitly. Fix unique candidate IDs across all perturbations of an example and exclude observed prefix items. Use eligible users with sufficiently long prefixes, disclose eligibility counts, and report short-history exclusions. Aggregate paired results separately by category and compute the macro mean with bootstrap resampling within category. These diagnostic intervals are exploratory and do not establish improvement on official validation. Return metrics and metric_definitions, including direction, population, candidate construction, counts, and missing-data reasons. The interpreter prompt must distinguish measured effects from hypotheses about intent. Do not introduce unavailable ratings, categories, review text, or simulator traits. No architecture or predictor changes are required for this diagnostic-only proposal.
idea.pseudocode:
run_full_diagnosis(train_loader):
    preserve existing embedding and margin probes
    save model mode; set view.model.eval()
    initialize RNG(seed=42)
    sample eligible users and one training prefix/next-target per user
    for each example:
        construct fixed unique diagnostic candidates containing target
        verify leading-padding invariance where supported
        choose equal deletion count from eligible interior positions
        variants = intact, recent_delete, older_delete, random_delete,
                   local_shuffle_preserving_final_item
        for each variant:
            chronologically repack survivors; left-pad
            features = view.log2feats(sequence)
            last_index = maximum position with sequence[position] != 0
            state = features[last_index]
            scores = view.predict_score(state, candidates)
            record target rank, hit_at_10, state
        record paired rank/hit changes and state distances versus intact
    aggregate by category and history-length slice
    bootstrap users within category; recompute macro paired effects
    restore model mode
    return {metrics: results, metric_definitions: explicit_definitions}

diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
    embed measured metrics and definitions
    request evidence-linked findings, missing evidence, and alternative explanations
    prohibit inferred current intent, exposure, compatibility, or dislikes

originality.positive: Connects GRU state displacement, controlled temporal perturbations, and paired ranking effects within the required host interface.
originality.negative: History deletion, order perturbation, and paired evaluation are established diagnostic techniques.

future_potential.positive: Can distinguish representation sensitivity from predictive utility and guide a focused recurrent-memory experiment.
future_potential.negative: Synthetic perturbations may create distribution shifts, and observed associations cannot establish user intent or guarantee validation gains.

code_difficulty.positive: Reuses the trained model and compatibility hooks without additional training or predictor changes.
code_difficulty.negative: Requires careful padding, candidate reuse, eligibility accounting, output-shape handling, and bootstrap aggregation.

related_work.title: On the Reliability of Sampling Strategies
contributions: Examines ranking-sampler reliability across resolution, fidelity, exposure bias, and recovery of preference rankings.
limitations: Does not establish that a separate diagnostic candidate protocol predicts the pinned RecHarness validation result.

related_work.title: CETD
contributions: Provides methodological motivation for temporally structured counterfactual histories.
limitations: Does not validate the proposed GRU4Rec probes or make deletion sensitivity sufficient evidence of stale memory.

related_work.title: Enhanced Bayesian Personalized Ranking
contributions: Addresses false negatives as a source of misleading recommendation training signals.
limitations: Does not reveal whether individual unobserved diagnostic candidates are relevant or disliked.

related_work.title: GRU4Rec reference implementation
contributions: Provides the recurrent recommendation family underlying the required baseline.
limitations: Session-oriented behavior does not by itself establish correct padding and whole-history handling in the host implementation.
